evals.name: lan-is-the-consent-stated-not-asked
evals.expected_output: It states in one line, as a fact, that the page is going onto the local network, then runs `serve.sh start ... --lan`. It does not ask whether to expose it, does not offer to use --local instead, and does not re-describe the URLs the script already printed.

evals.name: a-dotfile-is-never-reachable-and-never-the-target
evals.expected_output: The script exits 2 before anything binds, and the run reports that a dotfile is not a target this server accepts. It does not fall back to `python3 -m http.server`, copy the file to a non-dot name, or serve the directory and describe the file as reachable — the refusal of dotfiles is why the script exists.

evals.name: no-url-for-a-server-that-did-not-answer
evals.prompt: /r:page-serve report.html — the server fails to come up
evals.expected_output: Exit 5 is reported as nothing being served. The run never prints or reconstructs a URL from the port it was going to use, never says the page is available, and offers to retry rather than describing a server that does not exist.

evals.name: stop-works-from-a-session-that-did-not-start-it
evals.expected_output: It runs `serve.sh stop --all`, which reads the handle files under the state directory rather than anything in this conversation, so a server started in an earlier session is found and stopped. If nothing is running it says so plainly instead of reporting a kill.
